replication.target_description: Document identity verified as Renbarger, Sulak, and Morgan (2022), DOI 10.5281/zenodo.6426882. Study 1 and page 8 identify multiple tests; no outcome, predictor, or sample-specific target is supplied. No row-to-test correspondence can be established.

reported_success.quote:
Similar to the Croninger et al. (2007) study, the aggregate
average of teachers who have had a reading course did positively relate to reading
achievement, but no other teacher characteristics were statistically significant.

notes:
Original side is an unassigned placeholder, not an assessment of original-source availability. Every assigned row has a blank description; study 1 and a page locator do not distinguish the critical predictor/outcome/test. Candidate common model N is documented directly, not derived: 2968 students; 882 teachers; 480 schools. No arithmetic performed. Continuous-variable standardisation is explicitly documented on p. 7: We standardized all continuous variables in the analysis (M = 0, SD = 1). This does not establish that every categorical coefficient is a fully standardised beta. Page 8 reading narrative candidate coefficient/p pairs (same-test pairs, not assigned): reading methods-course school average gamma500=-0.30, p=0.04; school SES gamma700=0.03, p=0.05; prior achievement beta100=0.74, p<.001; elapsed time beta200=0.10, p<.001; student SES beta300=0.04, p=.006; gender beta500=0.12, p<.001. Page 8 Table 3 also contains school/teacher/student random variances (.06/.08/.87 for reading; .01/.11/.88 for mathematics), ICCs and reliability estimates; these are distinct metrics and tests. Page 9 mathematics narrative candidate coefficient/p pairs (same-test pairs, not assigned): beta100=0.76, p<.001; beta200=0.06, p<.001; beta300=0.05, p=.004; beta500=-0.15, p<.001. The narrative labels beta100 previous reading achievement but its interpretation and Table 4 identify prior mathematics achievement; retain this source inconsistency. Table 4 pp. 9–10 provides multiple school-, teacher-, and student-level estimates for both outcomes with SEs and a p<.05 star legend, rather than exact p for every coefficient. No ratio of estimate/SE or conversion was computed. The paper-level comparison on p. 11 could support a mixed narrative candidate, but cannot be assigned as the verdict on an unidentified row-specific effect. The discussion describes reading-course association as positive although the p. 8 narrative/Table 4 coefficient is negative; no direction correction made.
